newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes sell-off late in battle over data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes sell-off late in battle over data.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes weakened considerably late Wednesday, failing to hold earlier gains which were pegged to what many traders considered dubious inventory data showing strong gasoline demand.

June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing slid from nearly 20 cents higher at midday to 5 cents lower later in the session. Benchmark June WTI/Cushing talked at $19.55-65 a barrel, around 10 cents weaker than second month July outrights.

Meanwhile, domestic grades firmed for the majority of the session, pumped higher for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James barrels on sentiment there was not a lot of prompt foreign competition in the U.S. Gulf.

For outrights, the basis for morning and early afternoon buying were Tuesday evening's American Petroleum Institute (API) data, which showed gasoline stocks dropping 3.6 million barrels and implied demand of 8.7 million barrels per day for week ended May 2.
Earlier predictions that API numbers would fade became reality, deflating outright crudes, traders noted.
Deals for LLS/St. James reached a high point at WTI/Cushing +8 cents, moving back to sell at a 4 cents premium in late action.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire moved at discounts of 35 and 38 cents to the marker, slightly firmer than Tuesday.
Midland/WTI remained around a 30 cents discount, getting attention for deals at WTI/Cushing -30 and -29 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland talked late at minus $1.55-50, Eugene Island around last deals at minus $1.40 and WTI/Cushing Postings at $1.83-85, in the middle of trades at $1.84.
Crude traders said foreign barrels were being "slamdunked" in the U.S. Gulf, allowing the firming trend for sweet barrels.
Sour grades found support from concerns over threats to Canadian IPL pumping operations in Manitoba from recent disastrous flooding.
Heavy discounting and severe competition in most sour sectors also underpinned domestic differentials, traders said.
Overall, traders said the slight contango June finds itself against July should continue in the weeks ahead.

"The structure of the market looks to have a little contango in a flat market for 1997, with the perceptions that builds in PADD III (U.S. Gulf Coast) stocks will lead to larger builds in PADD II (U.S. Mid-Continent) later on," said a cash dealer.
Contango markets are a bearish indicator, with the front contracts trading at discounts to later months.
